question.text: For a particular reversible reaction at temperature $T, \Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ were found to be both $+v e$. If $T_e$ is the temperature at equilibrium, the reaction would be spontaneous when

solution.text:
$$
\Delta \mathrm{G}=\Delta \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}
$$
at equilibrium, $\Delta \mathrm{G}=0$
for a reaction to be spontaneous $\Delta$ G should be negative
$$
\therefore \mathrm{T}>\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{e}}
$$
